turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Northstar Health is moving 2,400 staff to our platform. Their tenant code is NSH-417, and the rollout owner is Dana Cho, not Dan Cole from procurement.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I will keep Dana Cho as the operational owner and Dan Cole only as procurement.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: They require SAML SSO, EU data residency, and a seven-year audit-log retention period. The security review is the critical path.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Which region and launch date should I track?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Use West Europe. The original target is March 3, with a 200-person pilot two weeks earlier.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Understood: West Europe, February pilot, and March 3 full rollout.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Legal has not approved the data-processing addendum, so March 3 is no longer realistic. Move the full rollout to April 14.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Does the pilot move as well?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yes. Run a 75-person clinical-operations pilot on March 24. Do not include payroll in the pilot.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I saw a note about Northstar Dental launching March 3. Is that related?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: No, Northstar Dental is a different customer. This account is Northstar Health, tenant NSH-417.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I will keep those similarly named accounts separate.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The 75-person pilot finished. SSO worked, but audit exports timed out for files over 500 megabytes.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Was the timeout a region or permissions issue?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Neither. Engineering traced it to synchronous archive creation and assigned fix ENG-8821.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Should April 14 remain the launch target?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Keep April 14 for now, but Dana wants a successful large export by April 7 as the go/no-go check.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I will track ENG-8821 and the April 7 export check.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: ENG-8821 passed with a 1.2-gigabyte export. Dana approved launch, but hospital training conflicts pushed it from April 14 to April 21.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: So the technical blocker is closed and only training changed the date.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Correct. Also, their billing contact changed from Dan Cole to Morgan Li, while Dana Cho remains rollout owner.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Should monthly invoices still go to procurement?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Send invoices to Morgan Li and copy procurement. Never put patient identifiers in support tickets.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Recorded: April 21 launch, Morgan on billing, and no patient identifiers in tickets.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Northstar Health launched on April 21 and adoption reached 86 percent after eight weeks.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Any post-launch changes to their requirements?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: They kept SAML and West Europe. Audit-log retention is still seven years, but exports now run weekly instead of monthly.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Who owns the weekly export review?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Morgan reviews billing only. Dana assigned the export review to security analyst Luis Ortega.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I will route export issues to Luis and rollout questions to Dana.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I coordinate appointments for my father, Roberto Alvarez. He prefers Spanish for medical conversations, though routine reminders can be in English.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: I will use Spanish for clinical discussions and English for simple reminders.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: His cardiology clinic is Lakeside Heart, and Dr. Mehta sees him on Tuesday afternoons. He is allergic to penicillin.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: I will keep the penicillin allergy prominent. How does he get to appointments?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Usually I drive him. If I cannot, book CityRide at least 48 hours ahead; do not use QuickCab because they missed two pickups.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Understood: Elena first, CityRide backup, and no QuickCab.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The February 18 cardiology visit moved to February 20 at 10:30 in the morning because Dr. Mehta is covering the hospital.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: That is a Thursday morning instead of the usual Tuesday afternoon.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Right. I cannot drive that day, so CityRide confirmation CR-9082 is booked for 9:40.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Should I remind Roberto about fasting?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: No fasting was requested. The clinic only asked him to bring his medication list and home blood-pressure log.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: I will not invent a fasting requirement.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Roberto's pharmacy changed from Green Cross on Oak Street to Harbor Pharmacy on Pine Avenue.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Is Harbor Pharmacy the one near the marina?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: No, that is Harbor Drugs. Use Harbor Pharmacy on Pine Avenue, phone ending 4419.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: I will distinguish Harbor Pharmacy from Harbor Drugs.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: They deliver on Wednesdays. Leave packages with the front desk, not outside apartment 6B.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Wednesday delivery to the front desk for apartment 6B.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: We tried text reminders, but Roberto ignored the short code because it looked like spam.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Would a phone call work better?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Yes. Call in Spanish the evening before, then send me an English text as backup.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Does that replace the old reminder preference?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: It does. Do not send Roberto automated text reminders anymore.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Updated to Spanish phone calls for Roberto and backup texts only to Elena.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The June follow-up went well. Dr. Mehta moved routine visits from every three months to every six months.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Should transportation and reminder rules stay the same?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Yes: I drive when possible, CityRide otherwise, Spanish phone reminder the night before, and an English backup text to me.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: Any change to pharmacy delivery?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Harbor Pharmacy still delivers Wednesday, but packages now go to the parcel room because the front desk stopped accepting medicine.

turns.speaker: Care Assistant
turns.text: I updated only the delivery location to the parcel room.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Our family is planning a summer trip. Jo wants beaches, our son Eli gets carsick on winding roads, and I need reliable Wi-Fi for one work call.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: So direct transport, beach access, and dependable internet matter.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: We first considered Madeira from July 12 to July 19, but the mountain drives may be hard for Eli.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Would a flatter destination work better?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Probably. Jo is vegetarian but eats dairy, and Eli has a serious cashew allergy. Peanuts are fine.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: I will not conflate the cashew allergy with a general nut or peanut allergy.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: We dropped Madeira and reserved Valencia for July 13 through July 20. The apartment is near Malvarrosa Beach.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Does the Valencia apartment meet the work requirement?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The listing says fiber internet, but I want the host to run a speed test before the cancellation deadline on June 1.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: How will you get from the airport?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Metro if everyone feels well; otherwise a licensed taxi. Avoid the scenic mountain day trip because of Eli's carsickness.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Valencia replaced Madeira, with flat transit and no mountain excursion.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Separate household update: the kitchen contractor, Blue Finch Renovations, starts May 6.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Is that the same company as Bluebird Plumbing?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: No. Bluebird only fixed the sink last year. Blue Finch is replacing cabinet doors and counters for 8,700 dollars.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Who needs access during the work?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Site lead Noor Patel has the lockbox code. The dog walker should use the side door and must not enter the kitchen.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: I will keep contractor access separate from travel plans.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The Valencia host sent a 310 megabit speed test, so keep the booking.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: And did the kitchen finish on schedule?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Mostly. A cracked counter delayed completion from May 17 to May 24, but Blue Finch did not charge extra.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Any trip schedule changes?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: My work call moved from July 16 to July 17 at 15:00 Central European Summer Time. The family will visit the aquarium then.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: I will reserve July 17 for your call and the aquarium outing.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Valencia worked well. We used the metro, Eli was not carsick, and the apartment internet handled my call.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Did the food allergy plan work?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yes. Restaurants understood the cashew allergy. One waiter initially heard peanut, but we corrected him before ordering.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: What should I remember for the next trip?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Choose flatter cities with transit, verify Wi-Fi, keep a written cashew-allergy card in the local language, and find vegetarian options for Jo.

turns.speaker: Avery
turns.text: Those are now the durable family travel preferences.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Cedar & Steam is opening a second cafe at 18 Willow Market. The first shop is on Cedar Street, so reports must keep the locations separate.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Willow Market will be location two and Cedar Street remains location one.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: The target opening is April 5. We budgeted 42,000 dollars for equipment and 18,000 for the fit-out.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Who supplies the new espresso machine?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Roastline Equipment supplies the machine. Roastline Coffee is an unrelated bean subscription we canceled last year.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I will distinguish the equipment vendor from the former coffee subscription.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: The city permit review is three weeks late, so April 5 is at risk.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Should staffing interviews pause?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: No. Continue interviews for one manager and four baristas, but make offers conditional on the permit.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: What hours are planned?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Weekdays 7 to 6, weekends 8 to 4. Do not copy Cedar Street's 6 a.m. opening because the market building stays locked.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Willow Market starts at 7 on weekdays and 8 on weekends.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: The permit arrived, but the electrician found an undersized panel. Opening moves from April 5 to April 26.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Does the electrical work change the budget?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Yes, add 6,400 dollars. To compensate, lease the second grinder instead of buying it this quarter.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Any supplier changes?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Roastline Equipment is still delivering the espresso machine April 15. Mina Shah accepted the manager role.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I recorded April 26, the panel cost, grinder lease, and Mina as manager.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: The Willow Market cafe opened April 26. The first weekend was busy, but oat milk ran out by noon.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Was that a forecasting or supplier problem?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Forecasting. We ordered based on Cedar Street's mix, but Willow sells 40 percent more oat-milk drinks.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: How should ordering change?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Raise the Willow oat-milk par from 12 to 20 cases and review it every Monday. Cedar Street stays at 12.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Only Willow changes to 20 cases with Monday review.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: After three months, Willow Market is profitable, but weekday afternoons are quiet.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Are you reducing hours?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Not yet. Starting August 11, test a 3-to-5 p.m. study special before changing the 7-to-6 weekday schedule.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Did the oat-milk adjustment hold?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Yes. Twenty cases is slightly high, so lower Willow to 18. Keep the Monday review and leave Cedar Street at 12.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I updated Willow to 18 cases and kept the location-specific controls.
